sections_target.text: Introduction

This document outlines the 
equipment inspection I3, which must be performed 
every five years 
as indicated by Y5 in the title block This document for the cranes 
at turbines hall of units # 1,2 & 3,4

The first draft initiated 
by eng. Eid 
Lotfy, tested by eng 
Ibrahem Youssef, 
revised by quality control eng Adel Abd- El kader El Nagar at EDEPC, 
accepted by eng 
Sayed Farag:
general director, and approved 
by eng. 
Mokhtar Abd El-Latif Mady: head sector of Ataka PS

This document is accepted by Eng. Samir Abdel Galil, EDEPC Inspection and Quality Control General Director, MPIS Coordinator, and approved by Accountant Mahmoud Suleiman, EDEPC Financial Supervision and Inspection, General Director of Quality Control and Head of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector.
Safety precautions

A work permit must be issued and the maintenance staff should carry the 
 suitable safety category
A safety fence with warning signs surrounding the work area is required

Wear the safety 
 and healthy equipment as safety helmet, safety shoes, safety belt ...etc.

Shut down the power 
 supply of the crane.

sections_target.text: Work to be carried out

Operate the crane, observe and hear the sound 
 of main hoisting, auxiliary hoisting, trolley, and crane travel motors
Grease motors bearing.

General 
 cleaning for all motor, and electronic control panel, resistors, by air 
 blower.

Check the 
 motors breakers for main hoisting, auxiliary hoisting, trolley and crane 
 travel and change the motors breakers if necessary.

Check the 
 main power supply line and change if necessary.

Check the 
 contactors, auxiliary contactors, timers and change if necessary.
Operate the crane for test.

Place a copy of the field test 
 results at the equipment data file.

uncertain_terms.note: Source approval block is garbled and truncated (mixed Arabic/English, broken syntax, ending 'السيطرة على قطاع الرأس'); translated as best as possible from the fuller wording used in FS-033/FS-034. EDEPC = East Delta Electricity Production Company.

Manifest language is 'ar', but only about 12% of the body characters are Arabic script; the body is predominantly English. The Arabic headings, labels and fragments were translated into English and the English body was carried over verbatim, including its spelling and grammar.
